faq.title: Before you hit publish.
faq.description: A few things to know. For the details, head to our documentation.
faq.1q: How do I create a developer account?
faq.1a: Choose Create account and an available sign-in method: Google, Discord or email. Verify your address if you use email. Return with the same sign-in method to find your workspace.
faq.2q: Can other developers access my projects?
faq.2a: Dashboard management is restricted to the signed-in project owner. Project keys are scoped to a specific project. Published metadata is separate from your private project information.
faq.3q: What if I lose my key?
faq.3a: Contact the developer who issued it. Manually issued keys are shown in full once; the dashboard keeps a prefix for management. A checkpoint key may still be available in the original browser session. Otherwise, the issuer can revoke it and issue a replacement.
faq.4a: The available support channels are listed below. For a script-specific license issue, start with the script’s developer.
faq.supportNone: No direct support channel is configured yet. You can consult the documentation for setup and troubleshooting.
faq.5q: What happens when I publish an update?
faq.5a: A licensed release follows the current validated build and keeps its loader URL. Users receive the update on their next successful load. A free listing is a snapshot: publish it again to update that public version. Code already running does not update automatically.
faq.6a: No. Issue keys directly from your dashboard or backend API, or publish a free script. Checkpoints are an optional way for users to obtain a project key through your own provider account.
faq.7a: Your readable original is stored privately, encrypted at rest, and remains available for editing or download. Obfuscation is optional and off by default: Standard transforms locals and strings; Strong adds virtualization and has stricter compatibility limits. Builds run locally without executing your code. Protection cannot prevent reverse engineering or guarantee every executor; test your release. A privileged operator can access stored content.

faq.8q: Which obfuscation level should I choose?
faq.8a: Start with Standard and test the delivered build. Strong can increase size and startup cost; it rejects generic for loops, including pairs/ipairs. Unsupported syntax or resource limits fail without silently publishing the original. Both options are free, subject to service limits; your private original is kept.
